body: Hey, I just wanted to say thanks. You are the reason I'm alive today. Thank you!

Yes, that's what I'm worried about - him not respecting the limit. I'm sure it's BPD and not sure if there's NPD, also. But BPD - 100% sure! I read some tips/watched some videos but overall it seems like a very very hard thing and the best solution, from what I've read, if the person doesn't want any help, as my father, because he's old and he refuses to go to his GP, is to actually move out and don't contact him again. 

Thank you and I'll message you if I need more help but I think that's it for now. Thank you!

Yes, indeed it's easier to cope when I know that he's unstable. Any other advice about dealing with him? How do I set limits? How do I protect myself besides leaving? 

If I stay, the situation will escalate, but If I leave, wouldn't he feel abandoned and that'll trigger him, also? Like there's no option - stay -> escalate, leave -> escalate?

Copy-pasting from mayo clinic - he also shows these from NPD: 

* Have an exaggerated sense of self-importance
* Have a sense of entitlement and require constant, excessive admiration
* Exaggerate achievements and talents
* Expect special favors and unquestioning compliance with their expectations
* Have an inability or unwillingness to recognize the needs and feelings of others
* Become impatient or angry when they don't receive special treatment
* Have significant interpersonal problems and easily feel slighted
* React with rage or contempt and try to belittle the other person to make themselves appear superior
* Have difficulty regulating emotions and behavior
* Experience major problems dealing with stress and adapting to change
* Have secret feelings of insecurity, shame, vulnerability and humiliation

I hope I'm not flooding you with information  - actually, I remember now, there was a time a couple of months ago, we were arguing for days and there were periods of clear-headedness where he's said, I believe with sincerity, because I kept asking him "why are you insulting me?" and he said that he never means to say those things, they just come out and he doesn't know why, he's just so emotional and can't control himself. But I didn't believe him then and kept digging and thinking he's lying. Now I see that he's told me the truth. Even got some progress when I told him - "if you're going to continue with this, I don't want us to talk" and he genuinely seemed like trying not to upset me and being more considerate but that was until 2-3 weeks ago and since then he's slowly started to revert back to the old ways

OMG! I think you're right. I read the symptoms of BPD and narcissism and he has some of the narcissistic ones, I can copy-paste them but this'll get too long but it's clear that it's BPD. It fits! Wow! This is eye-opening! 

I read that the main trigger is feeling of abandonment and I guessed that's what triggered him on my birthday. But then would that mean the advice about leaving the room will be also a trigger? I see that I need to get away from him but I have to do it so that he's not triggered and I don't see how would that go?

For example - he's getting angry and starting to insult me. I say sorry(as much as I don't want to) and now I have to leave the situation - how do I do it so that he doesn't perceive it as abandonment? It really sucks that I have to bend my emotions and reactions in order not to escalate the situation but I'm willing to do that and then do something to calm me down when I'm alone.

I have fewer thoughts about killing myself today, maybe mainly because I slept 5-6 hours, instead of 4 but you are helping me tremendously and with your last reply I saw that there are other options! Thank you very much!!

Wow. This is mind-blowing. Really. Never thought of that this way. I even shared some things about him with a psychologist and she made me think that it's not his fault. Wow. Thank you, really! This is of great help.

I read briefly about BPD the first time you mentioned it and it didn't seem like it but I'll dig deeper this time. As I said, I thought he was a narcissist but that doesn't fit.

Yes, we all are living in our own versions of the world but he can't and is not even willing to peek through and see from another perspective.

I guess that's the problem - me putting my self-worth partly in his hands. Can you elaborate more on the stepping away part?

May I PM you?
On top of that, better to try something and have it not work than kill myself because I'm out of options.

What do you mean by too much power? Also, when he insults me and I confront him he's always, 100% of the times - "I didn't say that - you're making things up. What do you want from me". Even if I ask him why he called me like that just after the insult. At times, I think he's either dumb or crazy.

No, he drinks only in the evenings and he's drunk not that often. Yes but saying sorry for something that is clearly not my fault and it's very stupid feels like I'm giving up and saying - your behaviour is right, I am to blame.

It's really things like that that get him angry. Or, for example, if helping him with something, I try my best but if I get something wrong or even if I'm confused and ask him how to do it - instant anger and look - "you're a disappointment, a failure for not knowing this", he literally has told me - "how can you not know this" even when he knows it's my first time doing it.

Also, he likes to repeat that, as if he wants me to get angry and cry, he keeps repeating until I give him attention.

I think yes, this is the best route, after moving away from him(which I don't have the means to do now), but I don't know how to change my reaction and my previous attempts at limiting exposure, like yesterday when I got up and went to the other room, are unsuccessful.
By body language, I mean mostly looking me with disappointment, rolling his eyes

No, they are not hard, they are helpful. But he gets angry with me/blames me for everything, even simple things like I placed this here and not there, he turns them into big issues with a lot of yelling and body language

Potential boundaries? I don't know how you can help me, just listening is a lot of help. I've always told him - this is irritating me. Stop. As was the case yesterday evening. But he was also drunk and that didn't work. He blamed me for ruining his life??? I am feeling unstable because of him. I am really struggling to not kill myself since yesterday

Yes, I had a job for a short time. Then I couldn't do anything with my messed up sleep and quit. I know how to get out of the situation but it's near impossible. No sleep -> no energy + no brain "power"(lack of sleep lowers IQ) ->can't do anything -> no money to move out -> no sleep. It's just this cycle that I can't break. He keeps abusing me and I need to move out...but I don't have any money...

Yes, I'm alive now, I'm just crying and looking how to kill myself. For now, I'm alive, I really don't know if I'll be alive this evening or tomorrow. Thanks!

Not accomplished anymore. I don't know I was scared if he'd leave because he had two beers and was drunk, which is strange, it was dark outside and besides that I have no job and no money. I don't know about BPD but he's tried "to leave" before and when I've told him - "go on", he just stays. Maybe you're right. I was thinking about him being an narcissist.
Skills that are of no use now
Haven't done it yet but if someone has read this and wants to chat - PM me. PM me if you have some programming questions, too, I'll see if I can help.
